alternative_explanations: The residual convolution path may already preserve enough current-item information.
Differences across categories may reflect dataset difficulty, initialization, or public-validation checkpoint selection.
Adding an embedding signal may change representation magnitude without improving item-feature alignment.
gap.cheapest_discriminating_test: Before training, compare candidate and control outputs on fixed synthetic histories with identical encoder states. Both added signals must have equal norms, while only the candidate signal retains coordinate alignment with the tied item embeddings. Then compare their independently fitted seed-42 four-category HR@10 under the frozen protocol.
predicted_observations: Observed: the audited seed-42 baseline HR@10 values are 0.648, 0.561, 0.486, and 0.684; their unweighted mean is 0.59475.

Source inspection: encode_sequence ends with compressed convolutional state and strictly preceding context, while scoring uses dot products with item embeddings. A harmful loss of current-item alignment is unmeasured.
Provisional prediction: an aligned current-item signal improves mean HR@10 by more than 0.005 over the baseline and exceeds an equal-norm, coordinate-rotated signal.
gap.suspected_capability: A small final representation signal aligned with the tied current-item embedding may help rank the next item. The supplied baseline establishes ranking performance, not this mechanism.
gap.task_context: The supplied evidence graph contains one current audited baseline Observation, no edges, and no declared revisions. Older memory cards include discarded recency, gating, readout, and compression candidates, but those decisions neither establish nor refute this distinct mechanism on the current model. No confirmation outcome or user-level slice is supplied.

method.cost: No new parameters. One additional item-embedding lookup and O(BLD) elementwise work per encode_sequence call; runtime is unmeasured.
insertion_points: model.py: NextItNetModel.encode_sequence, immediately after the existing blended representation
control-1.py: NextItNetModel.encode_sequence, at the same point
method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis: add 0.10 times a bounded, scaled current-item embedding to each valid final state. The generated control adds the same signal after a fixed half-width circular rotation of feature coordinates. Rotation preserves each signal's norm and item information while disrupting its direct coordinate alignment with the tied scoring embeddings.
prerequisites: Host source admission and CPU contracts pass before any fit.
Candidate and control use independent fresh initialization for each category at seed 42.
Host costing confirms that all required candidate and generated-control fits plus overhead fit the reserved budget.
tensor_constraints: Keep input IDs unchanged and encode_sequence output causal with shape [B,L,D], original dtype and device.
Compute the added signal from item_emb(seq), scaled by sqrt(D), bounded with the incumbent 4*tanh(z/4) form, and masked to zero at padding positions.
Use a fixed coefficient 0.10 in both arms. In the control, circularly rotate feature coordinates by floor(D/2) using concatenation; add no learnable parameters.
Retain the existing 0.85/0.15 current-state and strictly preceding-context computation, including its no-predecessor fallback.
Keep forward and score_candidates unchanged so both score the same final encoded representations.

alternative_explanations: Any gain could arise from changed representation scale or optimization rather than coordinate alignment.
The rotated control may interact differently with trained convolutional features despite its equal signal norm.
Seed-42 development results may vary with initialization and checkpoint selection.
correctness_checks: Verify edits in model.py and control-1.py are confined to NextItNetModel.encode_sequence.
On fixed synthetic tensors, verify candidate and control added signals have equal per-position norms and differ by the specified feature rotation.
Check dense, right-aligned, internally padded, singleton, and empty histories for finite masked outputs and unchanged input IDs.
Check future-token perturbations cannot affect earlier outputs, padding gradients are zero, and batch permutation equivariance holds before and after a synthetic update.
After a synthetic update, verify score_candidates equals item_emb(candidates) @ encode_sequence(seq)[0,-1] and forward uses those same representations.
Audit independent initialization, unchanged parameter count, and execution of the frozen training and evaluation protocol.
proposal.expected_primary_and_slice_effects: The provisional target is seed-42 unweighted mean HR@10 strictly above 0.59975, versus the observed baseline mean 0.59475, and above the generated rotated-signal control. Report all four category effects and available history-length slices, including regressions; no slice benefit is established in advance.
proposal.falsification_condition: Reject implementation validity if equal-norm rotation, causality, masking, or scoring checks fail. The ranking prediction fails if candidate mean HR@10 is at most 0.59975 or is at most the generated control mean. A qualifying seed-42 result remains provisional and does not establish the alignment mechanism.
guardrails: Paths are relative to model/: model.py and control-1.py. Preserve unrelated code, imports, helpers, configuration, and method signatures.
Preserve 200 epochs, 200 batches, evaluation every 5 epochs, patience 20, public-validation-only checkpoint selection, and independent per-category seed-42 initialization.
Preserve numerically stable pairwise BPR, evaluation seed 20260923, 1000 evaluation users, positive plus 99 unique negatives, and unweighted four-category HR@10 aggregation.
Do not shorten the protocol or tune using confirmation outcomes.

gap.task_context: Observed: the graph contains one current audited development observation and no edges or visible revisions. Its seed-42 HR@10 values are 0.648, 0.561, 0.486, and 0.684, with unweighted mean 0.59925. Source inspection shows a fixed 0.85 current-state and 0.15 strictly preceding-context blend. The supplied retrieval reports omitted counterevidence, so the visible graph does not establish a mechanism. Provisional explanation: different features may need different context weights.

method.cost: Add one hidden-width parameter vector per model and elementwise readout operations. Reserve 800000 GPU-budget units for all required fits and overhead; actual cost requires host verification.
method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis. Let u and c be the incumbent compressed current state and compressed strictly preceding mean, and let q=0.15*tanh(a) for a learned feature vector initialized to zero. Candidate output with predecessors is 0.85u+0.15c+q*(c-u), a bounded featurewise convex blend. The generated control uses the same parameter vector, initialization, and q but outputs 0.85u+0.15c+q*(0.85u+0.15c), testing common-mode feature calibration. Both use the incumbent current-only fallback without predecessors.

attrs.claim: In the frozen seed-42 public development readout, mean HR@10 was 0.590 for the content-conditioned gate candidate, 0.59475 for the incumbent, and 0.583 for the matched static-gate control. The candidate-control difference was +0.007, but the candidate-incumbent difference was -0.00475 and the preregistered 0.59975 target was missed. This does not establish useful content conditioning.

interventions.candidate: A zero-initialized causal gate convolution receives normalized block activation and scales the activated second-convolution output by 2*sigmoid(gate).
interventions.control: The same added convolution and multiplier receive ones_like of the normalized activation, making the gate content-invariant at a fixed position.

attrs.qualification: Single public development seed with validation checkpoint selection; category contrasts are dependent exploratory observations. No confirmation result was supplied.

alternative_explanations: Independent initialization, optimization, or public-validation checkpoint selection could create the seed-42 difference.

Category effects may differ: the candidate loses to the incumbent in Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl.

attrs.hypothesis: The +0.007 candidate versus static-gate development contrast could reflect content-dependent gating, but its mechanism and repeatability remain unknown.
attrs.qualification: Scoped source review and finite synthetic admission and training checks do not establish trained gate sensitivity, causal isolation, or held-out ranking benefit.

attrs.gap: No supplied direct test shows that the trained candidate gate changes with content at a fixed position while the trained static control remains invariant, or that this causes repeatable ranking improvement.
attrs.next_discriminating_experiment: Using selected development checkpoints, vary activation content at fixed positions and measure both gates. Check initial block-output equivalence to the incumbent and scoring identities after a nonzero update and save/load. Preregister independent-seed repeats and paired category HR@10 comparisons against both control and incumbent on a separate public validation split.
attrs.predictions: A useful content mechanism predicts trained gate sensitivity and a consistent ranking loss when content dependence is removed. Optimization or checkpoint effects need not reproduce that paired intervention effect or the +0.007 contrast across seeds.

attrs.qualification: Exploratory development distribution by total training history, not truncated model input length. No causal long-range deficit, new inference or confirmation evidence.

attrs.claim: The candidate adds a zero-initialized, bias-free, 0.1-scaled tanh projection of the normalized current-item embedding. The matched control applies the same-capacity projection to the normalized current encoder state. Source review and host method-scope admission support this implementation description; fixed-state branch-formula discrimination and causal isolation remain unverified.

Public seed-42 development mean HR@10 was 0.591 for the candidate, 0.59525 for the incumbent, and 0.593 for the matched control. Candidate differences were -0.00425 to incumbent and -0.002 to control; control minus incumbent was -0.00225. Candidate minus control by category was +0.008 Movies_and_TV, -0.012 Industrial_and_Scientific, -0.005 Electronics, and +0.001 CDs_and_Vinyl. Candidate minus incumbent was -0.015, +0.010, -0.012, and 0.000 respectively. These negative, mixed, and null contrasts are dependent slices of one development seed. Neither new arm cleared the host baseline-only promotion rule.

The negative aggregate and mixed direct-versus-state contrast are compatible with no incremental benefit from explicit item identity, sufficient identity in the incumbent, optimization or capacity effects shared by both arms, unequal source-tensor distributions despite normalization, changed gradients to the shared item embedding, or seed, checkpoint, and category variation. The historical local-difference failure is context, not replication of this mechanism.

Run the preregistered CPU diagnostic with a common nonzero projection: hold encoder state fixed, perturb current-item embedding, compare explicit branch formulas, and verify zero-initialization equivalence, masking, future-token invariance, and scoring identity after an update. A separately preregistered independent-seed study under the full frozen protocol should compare direct and state branches, measure input distributions and gradients, retain category and history slices, and include an embedding-gradient-controlled ablation. These tests are unexecuted.

alternative_explanations: The incumbent may already calibrate output features adequately through its encoder and tied item embeddings.
Category difficulty, independent initialization, or validation checkpoint selection may explain observed ranking differences.
Earlier residual comparisons may have failed because of their source signals or optimization, without testing output feature calibration.
gap.cheapest_discriminating_test: CPU only: assign the same nonuniform, nonzero gain vector to both arms. On fixed encoder states, verify that the candidate changes the compressed current-state contribution, while the control changes only the strictly preceding context contribution. A singleton history must change only in the candidate. Check causality, padding, and scoring identity after a synthetic parameter update. This establishes the computational contrast, not a ranking benefit.
predicted_observations: Observed: incumbent seed-42 HR@10 is 0.674, 0.564, 0.464, and 0.679 across the four categories; the unweighted mean is 0.59525.

Observed: the direct item-identity candidate on this incumbent was 0.00425 below the incumbent mean and 0.002 below its matched control. Its Industrial_and_Scientific slice gained 0.010 against the incumbent, while Movies_and_TV and Electronics lost 0.015 and 0.012; these slices are dependent parts of one development comparison.

Observed: the earlier local-difference candidate, tested on a different incumbent, was 0.01425 below that incumbent and 0.007 below its matched control. Its result does not transfer automatically to the current model.

Graph review: the supplied edges link proposals, methods, tests, and dependent observations; no SUPERSEDES or ALTERNATIVE_TO edge or retired revision is visible. Some historical readout hashes are unavailable, so they supply no mechanism conclusion here.
Provisional prediction: calibrating current encoded features may improve ranking beyond both the incumbent and a matched calibration of preceding context. No such benefit has been measured.
gap.suspected_capability: A small learned, featurewise calibration of the current encoded state may improve its alignment with tied item-embedding scores. This is an unmeasured hypothesis, not an established incumbent deficit.
gap.task_context: The incumbent produces causal encoder states, compresses current and strictly preceding context separately, and blends them at 0.85/0.15 before scoring. The graph's two failed development comparisons tested local-state difference and direct raw-item identity residuals, not featurewise calibration of the compressed encoded current state. Their failed advancement gates are counterevidence to those candidates, not refutations of this new mechanism.

method.cost: One hidden-width parameter vector per new arm, with elementwise operations over [batch, length, hidden]. GPU runtime is unmeasured. Reserve full frozen-protocol fits and confirmation overhead in the proposal budget.
method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis. Add a zero-initialized learnable feature vector g to each arm. Keep the incumbent output intact, then add 0.1 × tanh(g) × compressed_current in the candidate. The generated control adds 0.1 × tanh(g) × compressed_preceding_context only where a predecessor exists. Both use the same parameter count, initialization, coefficient, and final valid-token mask. Zero initialization makes each arm equal the incumbent before learning; a nonuniform gain distinguishes current-state calibration from context calibration.

The candidate trailed both comparators in all four categories and was ineligible for confirmation.
attrs.history_qualification: Supplied exploratory candidate-incumbent history bins include a null Movies_and_TV 1-5 HR@10 effect among 262 users, a +0.0107 Industrial_and_Scientific 1-5 effect among 280, and a -0.1075 CDs_and_Vinyl 21-50 effect among 93. attrs.qualification: One public development seed with dependent category and history slices; no confirmation. Failed advancement does not prove universal harm or refute the mechanism.

The source depth is the sole planned architectural contrast.

attrs.qualification: Exploratory development distribution by total training history, not truncated model input length. No causal long-range deficit, new inference or confirmation evidence.

attrs.claim: The candidate adds a zero-initialized, bias-free projected residual from the masked second-block output; the matched control uses the masked seventh-block output. Both completed audited fresh seed-42 development execution under the frozen protocol. Source admission and finite synthetic checks support the concrete intervention, not all-input semantics or causal isolation.

Seed-42 public development mean HR@10 was 0.59075 candidate, 0.59225 seventh-block control, and 0.59525 incumbent. Candidate effects were -0.0045 versus incumbent and -0.0015 versus control; control was -0.003 versus incumbent. Candidate-minus-control category effects were Movies +0.002, Industrial -0.006, Electronics -0.008, and CDs +0.006. Candidate-minus-incumbent effects were -0.011, +0.011, -0.013, and -0.005 respectively. Neither new arm qualified for confirmation.
attrs.history_qualification: Exploratory candidate-incumbent total-training-history slices have positive, zero, and negative effects. The 6–20 bin is positive in three categories and negative in Movies; the 21–50 bin is negative in three and null in Industrial. Longer bins have 0–26 users. Control-by-history contrasts are missing; these dependent slices are not independent replication or a causal history test.
attrs.qualification: One public development seed and no supplied confirmation result. The negative aggregate fails the selection gate and preregistered 0.60025 target, without proving universal harm or refuting the proposed mechanism.

attrs.hypothesis: The final encoder may already preserve early features; added capacity or altered gradients may drive either arm; second- and seventh-block state distributions may remain unequal after L2 normalization; and initialization, checkpoint selection or category mix may explain small mixed effects. Earlier direct-identity and local-difference failures are related negative development observations, not independent depth-specific tests.

attrs.measurement_gap: First, on fixed CPU states with identical nonzero projection weights and a fixed readout, perturb only the second-block state and then only the seventh-block state; check each explicit branch formula, zero-initialization equivalence, causal masking, and forward/scoring identity after a synthetic update. To test predictive value, preregister a multi-seed frozen-protocol candidate/control/incumbent comparison with paired category and history effects, tap-state distributions, and gradient diagnostics. No confirmation or final-test evidence is supplied.

gap.cheapest_discriminating_test: CPU only: hold normalized current and preceding states fixed and compare the three explicit masked readout formulas. The candidate must remove the preceding-context contribution, the generated control must increase it, and all three must agree when there is no predecessor. Verify causality and both scoring identities after a synthetic parameter update. This checks computation, not ranking benefit.
predicted_observations: Observed: incumbent seed-42 HR@10 is 0.674, 0.564, 0.464 and 0.679 across the four categories; the unweighted mean is 0.59525. Source inspection shows a fixed 0.85 current-state and 0.15 preceding-context blend.

Observed counterevidence: the direct item-identity candidate averaged 0.00425 below this incumbent and 0.002 below its matched control. Its category effects versus the incumbent were -0.015, +0.010, -0.012 and 0. The earlier local-difference candidate also failed its development gate on a different incumbent.

Provisional: reducing the final context contribution may improve ranking if that blend dilutes useful current-state information. Neither failed candidate measured this change. No supplied graph revision supersedes those results, and a failed selection gate does not refute a mechanism.

gap.task_context: The graph links each prior aggregate to its proposal through TESTS and to its mechanism comparison and dependent slices through PRODUCES. It declares no SUPERSEDES or ALTERNATIVE_TO edges and no retired revision. The current incumbent's optimal context strength has not been measured.

method.cost: No added parameters; the existing context calculation may remain for a minimal source change. Host costing must establish affordability.
method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis: change only the final masked readout for positions with a valid predecessor. The candidate uses 1.00 × compressed current state plus 0.00 × compressed preceding context; the generated control uses 0.70 × current plus 0.30 × context. The incumbent uses 0.85 and 0.15. Both changes move the context weight by 0.15 in opposite directions, keep weights summing to one, add no parameters, and retain the incumbent no-predecessor fallback.

attrs.claim: The proposed contrast changed the final readout with a predecessor from incumbent 0.85 current/0.15 context to candidate 1.00/0.00 and generated control 0.70/0.30. Host admission and completed development execution were verified for the new arms under the frozen protocol. These checks do not establish that context information, representation scale, and optimization were causally isolated.

Public seed-42 development mean HR@10 was candidate 0.573, incumbent 0.59525, and higher-context control 0.5915. Candidate minus incumbent was -0.02225; candidate minus control was -0.0185; control minus incumbent was -0.00375. Candidate minus control by category was Movies_and_TV -0.023, Industrial_and_Scientific -0.033, Electronics -0.023, and CDs_and_Vinyl +0.005. Candidate minus incumbent was negative in all four categories. Exploratory history-length slices include negative and zero effects; sparse long-history bins and absent control-by-history contrasts prevent a history-specific inference. Host eligibility for confirmation was false. This is one development comparison, not four independent replications or causal proof.

The negative directional contrast is consistent with useful preceding-context information, but altered representation magnitude or optimization and seed-42 validation selection are competing explanations. The higher-context control also fell slightly below the incumbent, so the data do not establish a monotonic benefit from more context. The original dilution hypothesis remains unconfirmed rather than universally refuted.

Next discriminating experiment: first compare all three explicit masked formulas on fixed current and predecessor states with zero, one, and multiple predecessors, including post-update scoring identities. If a new study is authorized, run independently initialized, paired multi-seed development fits at the preregistered 0.00, 0.15, and 0.30 context weights under the same frozen protocol, with a norm-matched readout contrast and control-by-history slices. Compare whether losses track context removal after matching representation scale, while reporting null and negative slices. No confirmation result is available for this round.

gap.cheapest_discriminating_test: On CPU, inspect the instantiated eight-block dilation orders and use fixed weights and synthetic sequences to check that changing a past token can affect only its position and later positions. predicted_observations: Observed: the audited incumbent has seed-42 HR@10 of 0.674, 0.564, 0.464, and 0.679; its unweighted mean is 0.59525. Source inspection shows the default dilation order [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8].
Observed counterevidence: the item-identity candidate was 0.00425 below this incumbent on mean HR@10. Its four category slices are dependent parts of that aggregate, not replications.

gap.suspected_capability: Refining short-range patterns after broad-context convolution may improve next-item ranking.
gap.task_context: The graph's TESTS edges attach failed development comparisons to their proposals; PRODUCES edges attach dependent category slices and provisional mechanism comparisons. method.cost: No added parameters or convolution calls at the default eight blocks; kernel sizes and the dilation multiset stay fixed. GPU runtime is unmeasured, so host costing must cover complete candidate and control fits and any required confirmation.
method.mechanism: Replace only the block dilation schedule. At eight blocks, use [1,2,4,8,8,4,2,1] for the candidate and [8,4,2,1,1,2,4,8] for the generated control. Both use the same dilation multiset, block count, kernels, parameters, and incumbent readout. For other block counts, repeat the respective eight-value cycle and truncate. The comparison tests ordering, while any ranking difference remains subject to optimization and checkpoint effects.

predicted_observations: Observed: the current seed-42 HR@10 values are 0.654, 0.579, 0.467, and 0.687; their unweighted mean is 0.59675.

Observed: the round-14 candidate exceeded its then-incumbent mean by only 0.0015 and missed its stated 0.005 advancement threshold. Movies_and_TV fell by 0.020, while the other three categories gained 0.015, 0.003, and 0.008. These slices are dependent parts of one development comparison.

Observed in source: the final block injects 0.1 times the strictly preceding state mean before normalization; the readout also blends 0.15 times a strictly preceding context mean. The graph's TESTS and PRODUCES relations attach comparisons and dependent slices to earlier proposals; it supplies no mechanism confirmation or superseding revision.
Provisional: reducing the first injection may improve ranking on the current dilation schedule. No supplied result tests that coefficient change.
gap.suspected_capability: Preserving more of the final block's position-specific state before normalization may improve next-item ranking.
gap.task_context: One falsifiable coefficient test on the audited round-14 model. Earlier item-identity and local-difference candidates missed their development gates on different bases; their outcomes are counterevidence to broad claims of benefit from added local signals, not tests of this coefficient.

method.cost: No added parameters or convolution calls. The candidate and generated control retain the same tensor operations as the incumbent; full frozen-protocol fit cost remains subject to host costing.
method.mechanism: Change only the coefficient of the final-block strictly preceding mean: candidate 0.0, generated control 0.2, audited incumbent 0.1. This symmetric coefficient contrast tests whether less pre-normalization context helps ranking. It does not by itself prove over-smoothing.

attrs.cheapest_discriminating_test: On CPU, hold final-block states fixed and compare the candidate and generated control with the same masked, strictly preceding mean and fixed 0.1 coefficient. Observed in model.py: the last block computes a masked strictly preceding mean but multiplies it by 0.0. The existing readout separately blends a post-normalization preceding mean at weight 0.15.

Observed historical evidence: the dilation-order candidate gained 0.0015 over its then-incumbent in development, while its Movies_and_TV slice fell 0.020. The item-identity and local-difference candidates fell 0.00425 and 0.01425 against their respective incumbents. attrs.cost: No new parameters or convolution calls. Both new arms add a masked prefix mean, tanh, and residual addition; full candidate and control fit costs and conditional confirmation costs require host costing before execution.
attrs.mechanism: At the final block, compute the mean of valid strictly preceding final-block states. Candidate: add 0.1 times tanh of that mean to the current final-block state before the existing final LayerNorm. Generated control: retain the unmodified LayerNorm output, then add the identical saved signal immediately after LayerNorm and before the existing context readout. Both arms keep the incumbent dilation schedule and readout. This isolates injection location computationally; a ranking contrast alone cannot prove why it occurs.
prerequisites: Host source admission and CPU contracts pass.
Each category and seed starts from an independent fresh initialization.
Host costing confirms complete frozen-protocol fits and reserved conditional comparisons fit the budget.
tensor_constraints: Use only valid positions strictly before the current position; the signal is zero when no valid predecessor exists.
Keep encode_sequence causal, finite, shaped [batch, length, hidden], and zero at padding positions.
Preserve forward consumption of encode_sequence and score_candidates = item_emb(candidates) @ encode_sequence(seq)[0,-1] after learning.
Keep block count, dilation order, embeddings, scoring, and all training helpers unchanged.

method.mechanism: At eight blocks, the candidate retains the masked output after block four and the generated control retains the masked output after block six. Each replaces the normalized final state supplied to the existing context and compression readout with 0.9 times that state plus 0.1 times its retained state normalized by the existing LayerNorm. The arms differ only in retained depth. Ranking effects remain provisional evidence about why the change works.

attrs.cheapest_discriminating_test: On CPU, hold block outputs fixed and separately perturb the masked outputs of blocks four and six. Verify that the candidate readout responds to block four and the generated control to block six, while both preserve masking, causality, and scoring identities. This verifies the computation; frozen development comparisons test ranking benefit.
predicted_observations: Observed: current seed-42 HR@10 is 0.665, 0.572, 0.477, and 0.685 across the four categories; the unweighted mean is 0.59975.
Observed in current source: the eight-block dilation order is [1,2,4,8,8,4,2,1], and the readout uses the final block state and a strictly preceding context mean.

Observed counterevidence on older models: the dilation-order candidate gained only 0.0015 mean HR@10 against its then-baseline and lost 0.020 on Movies_and_TV; the item-identity and local-difference candidates missed their development gates. Their category slices are dependent parts of their aggregates.

attrs.cost: No new parameters or convolution calls; each arm retains one masked intermediate tensor and makes one additional LayerNorm call and blend per position. GPU runtime is unmeasured. The 950000 budget must cover candidate and generated-control development fits, conditional confirmation fits, missing incumbent confirmation fits, and overhead.
attrs.mechanism: At eight blocks, the candidate retains the masked output after block four and the generated control retains the masked output after block six. Each replaces the normalized final state supplied to the existing context and compression readout with 0.9 times that state plus 0.1 times its retained state normalized by the existing LayerNorm. The arms differ only in retained depth. Ranking effects remain provisional evidence about why the change works.
prerequisites: Fix both retained depths and the 0.1 coefficient before evaluation.
Pass host source admission and CPU contracts before training.
Use independent initialization for each category and seed.
Confirm that complete frozen-protocol costing fits the budget.

tensor_constraints: Mask each retained state per position before readout and preserve causality.
For nondefault block counts n, use candidate index max(0, floor(n/2)-1) and control index max(0, n-2), with zero-based indexing. The indices coincide only for n=1 or n=2; at n=4 they are 1 and 2.
Preserve finite [batch,length,hidden] output, zero padding output and gradients, and empty-history behavior.
Apply the blend inside encode_sequence so forward and score_candidates use the same representation after learning.
Preserve score_candidates as item_emb(candidates) multiplied by encode_sequence(seq)[0,-1].

correctness_checks: Verify edits in model.py and control-1.py are confined to NextItNetModel.encode_sequence; preserve signatures, imports, helpers, and unrelated code.
At eight blocks, verify candidate and control retain masked blocks four and six respectively, with identical coefficients, parameter counts, and final-state normalization.
At one and two blocks, verify retained indices coincide; at four blocks, verify candidate index 1 and control index 2.
With fixed block outputs, verify both formulas and each arm's sensitivity to its specified retained depth.
Check empty, singleton, dense, and right-aligned histories; future-token invariance; finite outputs and gradients; zero padding gradients; and batch independence before and after a synthetic update.
Verify forward and score_candidates identities after an update, independent initialization per category and seed, and frozen execution manifests.
attrs.expected_primary_and_slice_effects: Provisional prediction: candidate seed-42 unweighted four-category mean HR@10 exceeds 0.60475, strictly more than 0.005 above the observed incumbent mean of 0.59975, and exceeds the generated control. Report all four category effects and any available history-length slices with counts. No slice improvement is established in advance.
attrs.falsification_condition: Reject implementation admission if retained-depth selection, causality, masking, finiteness, or scoring contracts fail. Reject development advancement if candidate mean HR@10 is at most 0.60475, does not exceed the generated control, or fails host eligibility. Apply the frozen confirmation procedure only if development qualifies. An aggregate gain does not prove intermediate-feature preservation.
guardrails: Revision of the prior design: correct the retained-index declaration. Candidate and control indices coincide only for one- and two-block configurations; at four blocks they are 1 and 2. Preserve all host correctness gates.
All change paths are relative to model/: model.py and control-1.py.

Preserve 200 epochs, 200 batches, evaluation every 5 epochs, patience 20, stable pairwise BPR, evaluation seed 20260923, 1000 users, positive plus 99 unique negatives, public-validation-only checkpoint selection, and unweighted four-category HR@10.
Cost all candidate and generated-control fits, conditional confirmation fits, missing incumbent confirmation fits, and overhead before execution; do not shorten the protocol.
Use public development results for selection and keep mechanism conclusions provisional.

attrs.claim: Seed-42 public development mean HR@10 was 0.59075 for the candidate, 0.59625 for the block-six control, and 0.59975 for the incumbent. Candidate minus incumbent was -0.009; candidate minus control was -0.0055; control minus incumbent was -0.0035. Candidate eligibility for confirmation was false.
attrs.history_qualification: Exploratory candidate-incumbent history slices contain positive, negative, and zero HR@10 effects. They use total training-history length, lack control-by-history contrasts, and have sparse long-history bins; they are not independent replications or evidence of a long-range mechanism.
attrs.qualification: One public development seed; negative aggregate and null category contrast are retained. No confirmation or final-test result and no universal-harm claim.
